title: Security of processing
legal_text: Taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risk of varying likelihood and severity for the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller and the processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk.

sub_clauses.title: Pseudonymisation and Encryption
sub_clauses.text: The pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data.

sub_clauses.title: Confidentiality and Resilience
sub_clauses.text: The ability to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services.

sub_clauses.title: Incident Recovery and Restoration
sub_clauses.text: The ability to restore the availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident.

sub_clauses.title: Evaluation of Effectiveness
sub_clauses.text: A process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures for ensuring the security of the processing.

title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
legal_text: In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the personal data breach to the supervisory authority competent in accordance with Article 55, unless the personal data breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.

sub_clauses.title: Breach Description
sub_clauses.text: Describe the nature of the personal data breach including where possible, the categories and approximate number of data subjects concerned and data records concerned.

sub_clauses.title: Contact Point
sub_clauses.text: Communicate the name and contact details of the data protection officer or other contact point where more information can be obtained.

sub_clauses.title: Consequences
sub_clauses.text: Describe the likely consequences of the personal data breach.

sub_clauses.title: Remediation Measures
sub_clauses.text: Describe the measures taken or proposed to be taken by the controller to address the personal data breach, including, where appropriate, measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects.

title: Reporting of major ICT-related incidents
legal_text: Financial entities shall submit to the relevant competent authority the following reports within the prescribed deadlines: an initial notification no later than 4 hours from the classification of the major ICT incident and not later than 24 hours from becoming aware, an intermediate report within 72 hours, and a final report within 1 month.

sub_clauses.title: Initial Notification
sub_clauses.text: An initial notification within 4 hours from the moment of classification of the incident as major, and no later than 24 hours from becoming aware.

sub_clauses.title: Intermediate Report
sub_clauses.text: An intermediate report within 72 hours from the moment of classification of the major ICT-related incident.

sub_clauses.title: Final Report
sub_clauses.text: A final report within 1 month from the moment of resolution of the major ICT-related incident.

metadata.domain: Digital Operational Resilience in Financial Services

title: ICT risk management framework
legal_text: Financial entities shall have in place a sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework as part of their overall risk management system, which enables them to address ICT risk quickly and efficiently and to ensure a high level of digital operational resilience that is proportionate to their size and overall risk profile.

sub_clauses.title: Framework Governance
sub_clauses.text: The ICT risk management framework shall include at least strategies, policies, procedures, ICT protocols and tools that are necessary to duly and adequately protect all information assets and ICT assets.

sub_clauses.title: Regular Review
sub_clauses.text: Financial entities shall review the ICT risk management framework at least once a year, as well as upon the occurrence of major ICT-related incidents.

title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures
legal_text: Member States shall ensure that essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage the risks posed to the security of network and information systems which those entities use for their operations or for the provision of their services, and to prevent or minimise the impact of incidents on recipients of their services and on other services. Taking into account the state of the art and, where applicable, relevant European and international standards, as well as the cost of implementation, the measures shall ensure a level of security of network and information systems appropriate to the risks posed.

sub_clauses.title: Risk Analysis Policies
sub_clauses.text: Policies on risk analysis and information system security.

sub_clauses.title: Incident Handling
sub_clauses.text: Incident handling and operational business continuity management.

sub_clauses.title: Supply Chain Security
sub_clauses.text: Supply chain security, including security-related aspects concerning relationships between entities and direct suppliers.

sub_clauses.title: Cryptography and Encryption
sub_clauses.text: Policies and procedures regarding the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption.
